name: Russia–NATO
summary: Suspected drones reported at RAF Lakenheath on 13 Nov, after Baltic drone alerts on 10–11 Nov; no Article 4 request
state: US Air Force security staff responded to suspected unauthorised drone activity at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk on 13 Nov; no damage was reported, the UK Ministry of Defence said the incident was resolved and the drones' origin is unknown (Kyiv Independent, citing AP). Overnight on 10–11 Nov drones entering from Belarus set off air-raid warnings across Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, and NATO jets failed to down one (Euronews). No Article 4 request, direct clash or attack on NATO territory was found as of 15 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Residents of the Baltic states and Poland may see air-raid alerts and brief airspace or airport restrictions; follow national civil protection guidance. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice for the latest on disruption.
rubric_hit: Watch: drone violations of NATO airspace (Baltics 10–11 Nov, Lakenheath 13 Nov); no Article 4 or attack

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
